questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following sets of organs belong to the circulatory system?
questions.explanation: Circulatory system has heart, blood and blood vessels. These parts move blood around the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following blood cells is without a nucleus?
questions.explanation: Platelets do not have a nucleus. They help in blood clotting.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which disease is caused due to deficiency or abnormality of white blood cells?
questions.explanation: Leukemia is related to white blood cells. It occurs due to abnormal WBCs.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many chambers are there in the human heart?
questions.explanation: Human heart has four chambers. They are two auricles and two ventricles.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the cause of systolic pressure on the wall of the artery during the contraction phase of ventricle?
options: Excessive pressure is created inside the heart
The artery contracts at the time of contraction of the left ventricle
Blood becomes thicker at the time of contraction of the left ventricle
Pressure produced in the left ventricle of the heart is transmitted to the artery
questions.explanation: Left ventricle creates pressure while contracting. This pressure passes to arteries as systolic pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A person feels thirstier, hungrier, dizzy, sometimes faints, has frequent urination and blurred vision. What is the problem?
questions.explanation: Thirst, hunger, frequent urination and blurred vision are signs of high blood sugar. This problem is related to diabetes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which test is appropriate to identify blockage in a coronary artery during pain in the heart?
options: test of blood pressure of heart
questions.explanation: Angiogram shows blockage in coronary arteries. It is used when heart artery blockage is suspected.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Saambhawi's bleeding did not stop after an injury. What is the reason?
options: lack of white blood cells in blood
lack of red blood cells in blood
questions.explanation: Platelets help blood clot. If platelets are low, bleeding may not stop.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Rasmila's grandfather has swelling and pain in joints and was forbidden to eat meat and legumes. What is the problem?
questions.explanation: High uric acid can cause joint pain and swelling. Meat and legumes are limited in this problem.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the main parts of the human circulatory system?
questions.explanation: Circulatory system includes heart, blood vessels and blood. It transports substances around the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does the heart do in the circulatory system?
options: Pumps blood through blood vessels to different parts of the body
questions.explanation: Heart pumps blood. Blood goes through blood vessels to body parts.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: About how much blood is present in a healthy adult body according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: A healthy adult has about 5 litres of blood. This blood circulates through the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the nature of blood mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Blood is slightly alkaline. Its pH is about 7.35-7.45.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What percentage of blood is plasma?
questions.explanation: Plasma makes about 55% of blood. It is the liquid part of blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What percentage of blood is made of blood cells?
questions.explanation: Blood cells make about 45% of blood. They include RBCs, WBCs and platelets.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main component of plasma?
questions.explanation: Plasma is mostly water. Water helps carry dissolved substances.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What pigment in red blood cells transports oxygen?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin is found in red blood cells. It carries oxygen.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which blood cells fight against disease-causing germs?
questions.explanation: White blood cells fight germs. They protect the body from diseases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which blood cells help in clotting of blood?
questions.explanation: Platelets help stop bleeding. They form clots at injured places.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is serum?
options: A type of red blood cell
A blood vessel carrying oxygen only
questions.explanation: Serum is plasma without fibrinogen. Fibrinogen helps in clotting.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the life span of red blood cells according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells live about 90-120 days. After that, they are replaced.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where are red blood cells formed?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells are formed in bone marrow. Bone marrow is inside spongy bones.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which condition is caused by deficiency of red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Anaemia happens when RBCs or haemoglobin are low. It reduces oxygen carrying capacity.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which are granular white blood cells mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Neutrophil, eosinophil and basophil have granules. So they are granular WBCs.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which are non-granular white blood cells?
questions.explanation: Lymphocytes and monocytes do not have granules. So they are non-granular WBCs.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where are platelets formed?
questions.explanation: Platelets are formed in red bone marrow. They help in clotting blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the life span of platelets?
questions.explanation: Platelets live about 2 to 3 days. Their life span is short.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: On what basis are A, B, AB and O blood groups distinguished?
options: Presence or absence of antigen A and antigen B on RBC surface
questions.explanation: Blood groups depend on A and B antigens on RBCs. Their presence or absence decides the group.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which blood group has both antigen A and antigen B?
questions.explanation: AB blood group has both A and B antigens. So it is called AB.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which blood group has neither antigen A nor antigen B on the RBC surface?
questions.explanation: O blood group has no A or B antigen. So it is called O.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why should blood group be confirmed before blood transfusion?
options: It changes the heart into two chambers
questions.explanation: Wrong blood transfusion can cause dangerous reactions. It may even be fatal.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where is the human heart situated?
options: Inside the thoracic cavity between two lungs, slightly to the left side
questions.explanation: Heart is in the chest cavity between two lungs. It is slightly towards the left.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is pericardial fluid used for?
options: It protects the heart from external shocks and injuries
questions.explanation: Pericardial fluid protects the heart. It reduces shock and injury.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the upper two chambers of the heart called?
questions.explanation: Upper chambers of heart are auricles or atria. They receive blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the lower two chambers of the heart called?
questions.explanation: Lower chambers are ventricles. They pump blood out of the heart.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle?
options: It pumps blood to various organs with greater pressure
questions.explanation: Left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body. So its wall is thicker.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the role of valves in the heart?
options: They prevent blood from flowing backward
questions.explanation: Valves stop blood from going backward. They keep blood moving in one direction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to lungs. It comes from the right ventricle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which blood vessels carry oxygenated blood from lungs to the left auricle?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from lungs. They open into the left auricle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What causes a heart attack according to the chapter?
options: Reduced or blocked flow of blood to the heart muscles through coronary arteries
Formation of pollen baskets in heart
questions.explanation: Heart attack happens when coronary arteries are blocked. Then heart muscles get less blood and oxygen.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Most arteries carry oxygenated blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which blood vessels carry blood from body organs back to the heart?
questions.explanation: Veins carry blood back to the heart. Most veins carry deoxygenated blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main role of capillaries?
options: Exchange nutrients, oxygen, hormones, enzymes, carbon dioxide and wastes with cells
questions.explanation: Capillaries are very thin vessels. They exchange oxygen, food and wastes with cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the pathway of systemic blood circulation?
options: Left ventricle -> body parts -> right auricle
questions.explanation: Systemic circulation goes from left ventricle to body and back to right auricle. It supplies blood to body parts.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the pathway of pulmonary blood circulation?
options: Left ventricle -> body parts -> right auricle
questions.explanation: Pulmonary circulation goes from right ventricle to lungs and back to left auricle. It helps oxygenate blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the normal adult blood pressure given in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Normal adult blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. 120 is systolic and 80 is diastolic.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What condition is called hypertension in the chapter?
options: When blood pressure exceeds the normal level such as diastolic above 90 mmHg
When uric acid is removed from blood
questions.explanation: Hypertension means blood pressure is above normal. Diastolic pressure above 90 mmHg is high.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is diabetes according to the chapter?
options: A disease caused by naked seeds
A condition in which glucose management by insulin is insufficient and blood glucose rises
questions.explanation: Diabetes occurs when insulin cannot control blood glucose properly. Then blood glucose rises.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the condition called when uric acid level increases in blood?
questions.explanation: Hyperuricemia means high uric acid in blood. It can cause joint pain and swelling.
